editor_note: Accurate, natural translation. Terms are correct and used the same way throughout: "valores esperados", "propagación de Pauli", "acotar de forma más precisa la sensibilidad a los errores" and "Cancelación Probabilística de Errores (PEC)". It keeps the informal "Consulta" form.

Rewritten entry 21 is faithful and natural: "Copia y guarda el token al portador devuelto" and "incluyendo el CRN y el token al portador en los encabezados de la solicitud" say what the English says, and "token al portador" matches the term introduced in entry 20.

Faithful and natural, with consistent tú register: "restricciones basadas en contexto" is used for the term every time, the role conditions in [5] are kept exactly (Administrador/Editor/Visor, "solo puede añadir zonas de red"), and [4] keeps both the point that the restrictions do not grant access ("no asignan acceso") and the compromised-credentials caveat.

Rewritten entry 15 is faithful, including the caveat "ningún otro trabajo puede ejecutarse, incluidos los trabajos de calibración" and "algoritmos variacionales", and it keeps the file's "session"/"trabajo" convention ("Usar sessions").

None of the four rewritten entries (4, 7, 12, 15) would mislead a learner. The note in entry 4 keeps the "experimental", "preview" and "subject to change" caveats. The circuit function vs. application function table in entry 7 is faithful. The claims about ZNE/PEC, QESEM and HI-VQE in entries 12 and 15 keep their direction and scope, including "respectivamente, en órdenes de magnitud". Four small editorial slips remain. In entry 15, the QUICK-PDE row uses the acronym two ways within the same row: "EDP multifísicas" and then "soluciones de PDE". Also in entry 15, "optimized execution strategies and optimizers" became "estrategias de ejecución y optimizadores avanzados", so "optimized" is softened to "advanced". In entry 12, "primitivos Sampler y Estimator" uses the wrong gender (the usual term is "primitivas"), and "para entregar resultados precisos" is a calque of "deliver".

examples.source: Use quantum computation for multi-physics PDEs. ... delivers precise, scalable PDE solutions
examples.translation: Usa computación cuántica para EDP multifísicas. ... proporciona soluciones de PDE precisas y escalables
examples.suggested: ... soluciones de EDP precisas y escalables
examples.why: The same acronym appears in two forms in one table cell (EDP, then PDE), so the reader may wonder whether they mean the same thing.

examples.source: using optimized execution strategies and optimizers
examples.translation: usando estrategias de ejecución y optimizadores avanzados
examples.suggested: usando estrategias de ejecución y optimizadores optimizados/especializados
examples.why: 'Optimized' became 'avanzados', which slightly changes the claim. The meaning is still harmless.

examples.source: for the Sampler and the Estimator primitives
examples.translation: para los primitivos Sampler y Estimator
examples.suggested: para las primitivas Sampler y Estimator
examples.why: Spanish Qiskit material conventionally uses the feminine 'primitivas'.

examples.source: maximizing the performance of IBM devices to deliver accurate results
examples.translation: maximizando el rendimiento de los dispositivos IBM para entregar resultados precisos
examples.suggested: maximizando el rendimiento de los dispositivos IBM para obtener resultados precisos
examples.why: 'Entregar resultados' is a calque of 'deliver results'. A native writer would use 'obtener' or 'ofrecer'.

editor_note: Entries 25 and 26 match the English: "ventana de uso móvil de 28 días" is the same term used in entry 13, the limited-instance rule (pending work stays "en la cola", active work "continuará ejecutándose, incluidas las cargas de trabajo en modo de sesión") is correct, and the non-limited case keeps its hedge "es probable que ... menor prioridad".

Faithful, natural tú-register rendering with no drift; the entries keep the IDP/SSO terms ("proveedor de identidad externo (IDP)", "inicio de sesión único (SSO)"), the "(puede generar un costo)" caveat and the dynamic-rules tip ("reglas dinámicas para no tener que agregar manualmente cada usuario").

The meaning is faithful throughout, and no sentence would mislead a learner. The main problem is that the results table in [89] was left entirely in English ("Get register data", "Post-process the array manually", "per register", "Automatic", "Undo measurement twirling"), while the similar table in [23] was translated. 'Post-processing' appears three ways: "procesamiento posterior" in [13]/[72], "post-procesamiento" in [88] and "posprocesamiento" in [90]. 'Job' is "trabajo" everywhere except "job" in [97], and the headings switch from infinitives (Pasos 1-6) to imperatives in [86], [92] and [97]. There are also smaller slips: "valores de expectativa" is a calque (the usual term is "valores esperados"), [73] has the ungrammatical "cómo se dan forma", and [101] says "helper" where "asistente" or a rephrase would be expected.

examples.source: | Get register data | ... | Counts dictionary | ... Post-process the array manually | ... Automatic
examples.translation: | Get register data | ... | Counts dictionary | ... Post-process the array manually | ... Automatic
examples.suggested: | Obtener los datos del registro | ... | Diccionario de conteos | ... Posprocesa el array manualmente | ... Automático
examples.why: Only the header row was translated. The rest of the prose in the table is still English, unlike the translated table in [23].

examples.source: rewrite get_counts-based post-processing as NumPy operations
examples.translation: reescribe el post-procesamiento basado en get_counts
examples.suggested: reescribe el posprocesamiento basado en get_counts
examples.why: The same concept appears as 'procesamiento posterior' in [13]/[72] and 'posprocesamiento' in [90]. It should be one form, and 'posprocesamiento' is the RAE-preferred spelling.

examples.source: Estimator computes expectation values rather than returning raw samples
examples.translation: Estimator calcula valores de expectativa en lugar de devolver muestras sin procesar
examples.suggested: Estimator calcula valores esperados en lugar de devolver muestras sin procesar
examples.why: 'Valores de expectativa' is a calque. The usual Spanish term is 'valores esperados', and the same calque appears again in [64].

examples.source: choices that affect how the job results are shaped and post-processed
examples.translation: las decisiones que afectan cómo se dan forma y se procesan posteriormente los resultados del trabajo
examples.suggested: las decisiones que afectan a la forma y al posprocesamiento de los resultados del trabajo
examples.why: 'Se dan forma' is ungrammatical (it should be 'se da forma a'), and the whole clause is a stiff calque of the English.

examples.source: Full example: Migrate a basic sampling job
examples.translation: Ejemplo completo: Migra un job de muestreo básico
examples.suggested: Ejemplo completo: Migrar un trabajo de muestreo básico
examples.why: Everywhere else the file says 'trabajo' for job. This heading also uses an imperative, while the step headings in [34]-[83] use infinitives ([86] and [92] use imperatives too).

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally, with a consistent informal register ("Ejecuta solo la cantidad de shots que necesitas", "considera usar `NoiseLearner`"). It also keeps the source's stale-noise-model caveat intact ("solo es práctico si no hay una demora prolongada entre trabajos (por ejemplo, dentro de una sesión)").

The three rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally: entry 6 "Versiones de los paquetes"; entry 10 keeps boosting/bagging/stacking, uses "eigensolver cuántico variacional (VQE)" and "algoritmo cuántico de optimización aproximada (QAOA)", and keeps all three goals (diversidad, capacidades de generalización, complejidad general); entry 29 renders the "Paso 1" import/generate/split sequence correctly.

The rewrite of entry 19 is faithful and reads naturally: "que es el orden inverso al de la forma de la matriz subyacente" keeps the caveat that the (input_dim, output_dim) tuple is the reverse of the matrix shape, and it keeps the informal "puedes usar".

Entries 64 and 65 are faithful and natural: "Revisa la API del [Estimator de `qiskit-ibm-runtime`]" and "Revisa la API del [Sampler de `qiskit-ibm-runtime`]" use informal tú, keep Estimator/Sampler in English, and follow the same pattern as entries 61 and 62 ("Revisa la API de las primitivas de ...").

Faithful and natural throughout: the deprecation timeline in [3] (quedado obsoleto, se eliminará a principios de 2025 / en Qiskit SDK v2.0.0), fractional gates as "puertas fraccionarias" and flag as "indicador" all hold up, and "schedules de pulso" stays in English the same way everywhere.

Both rewritten entries read naturally and match the English. Entry 3 renders "readily deployable" as "se pueden desplegar fácilmente" and "addons" as "complementos de Qiskit", and entry 19 reuses "dinámica hamiltoniana AQC + Trotter" exactly as entries 8 and 11 do.

Both rewritten entries match their English in meaning, read naturally and use informal tú. Entry 18 renders "full details" as "Consulta ... para ver todos los detalles de la clase". Entry 25 moves the negation to the front ("No es necesario instanciar la clase de opciones de la primitiva ... si estás estableciendo opciones después de inicializar la primitiva") and keeps the condition intact.
Rewritten entry 8 renders "dynamical decoupling" as the standard Spanish term "desacoplamiento dinámico", keeps the link URL intact and matches the source's meaning.

None of the 9 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The twirling precedence rule in [21] and the Recommendations list in [105] keep their meaning, "shot" stays consistent with the rest of the page, and the register uses tú ("Revisa", "Encuentra", "Aprende"). One thing a native physics editor would change: entry [58] renders "ground state" as "estado base", a calque. The standard Spanish physics term is "estado fundamental". Optionally, "Documentación de API de X" in the repeated link labels reads a little more naturally as "Documentación de la API de X", but the current wording is defensible.

examples.source: Whether to reset the qubits to the ground state for each shot.
examples.translation: Si se deben restablecer los qubits al estado base para cada shot.
examples.suggested: Si se deben restablecer los qubits al estado fundamental en cada shot.
examples.why: The standard Spanish physics term for 'ground state' is 'estado fundamental'. 'Estado base' is a recognizable calque that could be confused with 'estado de la base' (basis state). This is minor and does not change the meaning.

editor_note: Nothing in the translation would mislead a reader. The encryption-at-rest claim, the Manager-role condition and the three-year retention caveat "(no eliminados)" all match the English. Two small fixes are still worth making. In [7], "Eliminar una instancia de servicio elimina..." repeats the verb awkwardly, and the comma has slipped inside the link text: "[página de Instancias,]". In [0], "users" was dropped, so the sentence now says that customers ("los clientes") delete their own data.

examples.source: Deleting a service instance removes all of the content associated with that instance ... from the [Instances page](...), find the instance
examples.translation: Eliminar una instancia de servicio elimina todo el contenido ... desde la [página de Instancias,](...) encuentra la instancia
examples.suggested: Al eliminar una instancia de servicio se borra todo el contenido ... desde la [página de Instancias](...), busca la instancia
examples.why: Repeating eliminar/elimina reads like a word-for-word calque, and the comma belongs outside the link text.

examples.source: How customer data is encrypted and how users can delete their personal data.
examples.translation: Cómo se cifran los datos de los clientes y cómo pueden eliminar sus datos personales.
examples.suggested: Cómo se cifran los datos de los clientes y cómo los usuarios pueden eliminar sus datos personales.
examples.why: Without 'los usuarios', the subject is taken from 'clientes'. That is a small change in who the sentence is about, but it does not mislead.

editor_note: Both rewritten code-comment headings are faithful. "Obtener los argumentos del programa" (entry 12) and "Distribuir la tarea entre los trabajadores" (entry 14) match their English sources, and "trabajadores" is a defensible rendering of "workers".

The Spanish keeps the meaning and reads naturally, with correct terms like "mediciones proyectivas", "teorema de no clonación" and "distinguir perfectamente estados cuánticos no ortogonales", and it uses the informal "te guía" and "Descarga" throughout.

Both rewritten entries are faithful and natural. In entry 96, "€93B" becomes "93 000 millones de euros", the correct long-scale value, and the date is "17 dic. 2025". In entry 117, the date is "19 ago. 2025" and the gloss reads "revisión comparativa que incluye la estrategia de hardware y el ecosistema de IBM", which keeps the English meaning.

The translation is faithful and reads naturally, with "kick-start quantum initiatives" rendered as "poner en marcha iniciativas cuánticas con éxito", "startup leadership" as "equipos directivos de startups", and the informal "tú" used throughout ("Si tienes preguntas... contacta").

The page is faithful and uses tú throughout. The key facts are correct: 20 questions, at least 16 to pass, and a temporary lock after two failed attempts. In [11], "for program reporting and operational purposes" became "con fines programáticos y operativos". That drops the reporting purpose, and "programáticos" is a calque that means something different in Spanish. Also in [11], "to assist in the administration" became "para administrar", which makes Credly's role sound bigger than it is. In [7], "badging exam" became "examen final", which loses the link between the exam and the badge.

examples.source: Your personal information is used to issue your badge and for program reporting and operational purposes.
examples.translation: Tus datos personales se utilizarán para la emisión de tu insignia y con fines programáticos y operativos.
examples.suggested: Tus datos personales se utilizarán para emitir tu insignia y con fines de informes del programa y operativos.
examples.why: This drops 'reporting', and 'programáticos' is a calque that doesn't mean 'related to the program' in Spanish.

examples.source: to assist in the administration of the IBM Digital Badge program
examples.translation: para administrar el programa IBM Digital Badge
examples.suggested: para ayudar en la administración del programa IBM Digital Badge
examples.why: This makes the claim stronger than the source: in English Credly only assists with running the program, but the Spanish says Credly runs it.

examples.source: where you can take the badging exam for Foundations of quantum error correction
examples.translation: donde podrás realizar el examen final de Fundamentos de la corrección de errores cuánticos
examples.suggested: donde podrás realizar el examen para obtener la insignia de Fundamentos de la corrección de errores cuánticos
examples.why: 'Examen final' loses the source's point that this is the exam that earns the badge.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and the core terms are correct and consistent (códigos correctores de errores cuánticos, código tórico, códigos de superficie, códigos de color). In [2], "Corregir un error en cinco, siete o nueve qubits" drops the "one qubit out of" ratio. That ratio is exactly why the English calls these codes low-tolerance, so the point comes through weaker, though the reader is not actively misled. There are also a few calques and some stiff phrasing: "un problema con ellos es que", "Alternativamente", "discute" for "discusses" in the video title, and the awkward trailing adjective in "la corrección de errores cuánticos práctica".

examples.source: Correcting an error on one qubit out of five, seven, or nine isn't bad
examples.translation: Corregir un error en cinco, siete o nueve qubits no está mal
examples.suggested: Corregir un error en un solo qubit de cada cinco, siete o nueve no está mal
examples.why: This drops the 'one out of n' ratio, which is what makes these codes' error tolerance low.

examples.source: promising candidates for practical quantum error correction
examples.translation: candidatos prometedores para la corrección de errores cuánticos práctica
examples.suggested: candidatos prometedores para una corrección práctica de errores cuánticos
examples.why: Putting 'práctica' after the long noun phrase is clumsy. It also reads as if it modifies 'errores cuánticos'.

examples.source: John Watrous discusses CSS codes, Toric codes, and other code families
examples.translation: John Watrous discute los códigos CSS, los códigos tóricos y otras familias
examples.suggested: John Watrous presenta los códigos CSS, los códigos tóricos y otras familias
examples.why: 'Discutir' calques the English 'discuss' and in Spanish can suggest arguing. 'Presenta', 'explica' or 'analiza' reads more naturally.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and the core terms are correct and consistent: formalismo de estabilizadores, códigos de estabilizador, observables, código de repetición, tú register. Entry [3] has a stiff calque, "Esto tanto informará como conducirá a una discusión general". It copies the English "both inform and lead into", and a native technical writer would not phrase it that way. In entry [6], "are reviewed" becomes "Se tratan", which loses the sense that this is a review of earlier material ("se repasan").

examples.source: This will both inform and lead into a general discussion of stabilizer codes
examples.translation: Esto tanto informará como conducirá a una discusión general de los códigos de estabilizador
examples.suggested: Esto servirá de base y de transición hacia un análisis general de los códigos de estabilizador
examples.why: This copies the English 'both X and Y' structure, and 'discusión' is a calque of 'discussion'. It reads as translationese.

examples.source: Pauli operations and observables are reviewed.
examples.translation: Se tratan las operaciones de Pauli y los observables.
examples.suggested: Se repasan las operaciones de Pauli y los observables.
examples.why: 'Reviewed' means the material has been seen before. 'Se tratan' loses that and makes it sound like new material.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The terms are right: estimación de fase, transformada cuántica de Fourier, algoritmo de Shor, factorización de enteros. Two phrasings would read better to a native editor. In the video title [6], "se dirige al algoritmo de Shor" is a stiff rendering of "moves on to" and should be "pasa al algoritmo de Shor". In [5], the link "Descargar diapositivas" uses the infinitive, which breaks from the tú voice used elsewhere ("puedes abrir"); "Descarga las diapositivas" would match.

examples.source: With this in hand, John moves on to Shor's algorithm.
examples.translation: A partir de ahí, se dirige al algoritmo de Shor.
examples.suggested: Con esto, pasa al algoritmo de Shor.
examples.why: 'Dirigirse a' means to physically head somewhere or to address someone. For moving on to the next topic, the natural verb is 'pasar a'.

examples.source: [Download the slides] for this lesson.
examples.translation: [Descargar diapositivas] de esta lección.
examples.suggested: [Descarga las diapositivas] de esta lección.
examples.why: This bare infinitive reads like a button label and drops the article. The imperative keeps the informal tú voice of the rest of the sentence.

editor_note: I checked the four rewritten entries (4, 7, 21, 64) against the English and none of them would mislead a learner. The range 0 to 1, orthogonal states giving 0, "salvo una fase global" and the "máximo producto interno (en valor absoluto)" wording of Uhlmann's theorem all match the source. Two phrasings would still get a native editor's touch. In entry 64, "cualesquiera dos estados cuánticos" copies the English word order, where "dos estados cuánticos cualesquiera" is the natural Spanish. In entry 7, "y quizás no fácil de manejar" drops the verb and reads clipped; "y quizás no sea fácil de manejar" fixes it.

examples.source: the fidelity between any two quantum states is equal to the *maximum* inner product
examples.translation: la fidelidad entre cualesquiera dos estados cuánticos es igual al *máximo* producto interno
examples.suggested: la fidelidad entre dos estados cuánticos cualesquiera es igual al *máximo* producto interno
examples.why: This copies the English word order. In Spanish, 'cualesquiera' normally comes after the noun, as in 'dos estados cualesquiera'.

examples.source: might look unusual or mysterious, and perhaps not easy to work with.
examples.translation: puede parecer inusual o enigmática, y quizás no fácil de manejar.
examples.suggested: puede parecer inusual o enigmática, y quizás no sea fácil de manejar.
examples.why: The clause has no verb, so it reads clipped. After 'quizás', Spanish uses the subjunctive: 'quizás no sea fácil de manejar'.

editor_note: Faithful and natural Spanish that keeps every point of the source. Mappings become the standard math term "aplicaciones", channels become "canales", the discrete-time tooltip becomes "en tiempo discreto", and the informal tú holds throughout ("te guía", "puedes abrir", "Descarga").

Entry 35's video title is faithful and reads naturally. "El Director de Investigación de IBM, Darío Gil, contrasta la unidad principal de información clásica (bit) con la unidad principal de información cuántica (qubit)" matches both the English and the wording of entry 34.

Entry 16 is faithful and complete. It renders "third-party data processor" with the correct legal term "encargado del tratamiento de datos externo", keeps the data list (nombre, correo electrónico, insignia obtenida) and the "puede compartir … a nivel mundial" caveat, and uses tú throughout (emitirte, Recibirás).

All three rewritten entries (43, 48, 50) are faithful and natural, in tú register: "Lee las preguntas… haz clic en los triángulos", "las respuestas completas deben incluir lo siguiente", and "evita el costoso cálculo de elementos de matriz mediante la prueba de Hadamard", which keeps the "much less QPU time" claim and its reason intact.

Nothing here would mislead a learner, and the informal tú register holds throughout ("Aprende", "realiza", "tus datos"). A native editor would still change three things. First, "machine learning" is rendered as "aprendizaje automático" in [0] but left as the English "Machine Learning" three times in [4]. Second, "consistent with IBM privacy practices" becomes the calque "de manera consistente con" in [11]. Third, "third-party data processor" is flattened to "proveedor externo", which loses the data-processor role that matters in this privacy notice.

examples.source: how quantum computing can play an exciting role in machine learning
examples.translation: en el campo del Machine Learning
examples.suggested: en el campo del aprendizaje automático
examples.why: Entry [0] uses 'aprendizaje automático', but [4] switches to the English 'Machine Learning' three times, so the same term appears two ways within the page.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Serán tratados de manera consistente con las prácticas de privacidad de IBM.
examples.suggested: Se tratarán conforme a las prácticas de privacidad de IBM.
examples.why: 'Consistente con' is a calque of 'consistent with'. In legal and privacy text, idiomatic Spanish uses 'conforme a' or 'de acuerdo con'.

examples.source: a third-party data processor authorized by IBM
examples.translation: un proveedor externo autorizado por IBM
examples.suggested: un encargado del tratamiento de datos externo autorizado por IBM
examples.why: The data-processor role is dropped. This is a minor loss of precision in a privacy notice, not a misleading claim.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the GHZ accidental-protection argument ([137]-[152]) and the DD caveats ([44]-[48]). I found no drift or invented claims. "Expectation value" is rendered throughout as the calque "valor de expectativa", where the standard Spanish physics term is "valor esperado". "Stochastic decay" became "desintegración estocástica", which suggests radioactive disintegration rather than decay of the signal ("decaimiento"). Two phrases also read stiffly: "ruido de este tipo de desfase" and "no se pueden hacer twirling por completo".

examples.source: We calculate the average `X` expectation value across multiple qubits.
examples.translation: Calculamos el valor de expectativa promedio de `X` a través de varios qubits.
examples.suggested: Calculamos el valor esperado promedio de `X` en varios qubits.
examples.why: 'Valor esperado' is the standard Spanish term. 'Valor de expectativa' is an English calque, and it is used throughout the file ([57], [66], [69], [113], [119]).

examples.source: converts that coherent buildup into stochastic decay
examples.translation: convierte esa acumulación coherente en una desintegración estocástica
examples.suggested: convierte esa acumulación coherente en un decaimiento estocástico
examples.why: 'Desintegración' means disintegration or radioactive decay. For a decaying signal or fidelity, the usual word is 'decaimiento'.

examples.source: If there is more such dephasing noise, the phase will be less well-defined.
examples.translation: Si hay más ruido de este tipo de desfase, la fase estará menos bien definida.
examples.suggested: Cuanto mayor sea este ruido de desfase, menos definida estará la fase.
examples.why: 'Ruido de este tipo de desfase' is a clumsy calque, and 'menos bien definida' is stiff.

examples.source: some single-qubit gates are non-Clifford, which cannot be fully twirled
examples.translation: algunas puertas de un solo qubit son no-Clifford, las cuales no se pueden hacer twirling por completo
examples.suggested: algunas puertas de un solo qubit no son de Clifford, y a ellas no se les puede aplicar twirling por completo
examples.why: 'No se pueden hacer twirling' is ungrammatical. It needs 'aplicar twirling a'.

editor_note: One claim is strengthened. In [9], "increasingly advanced forms of error correction are steadily coming within reach" becomes "están al alcance de la mano", which says advanced error correction is already readily available instead of gradually getting closer. In [4], "compared with classical methods alone" becomes "en comparación únicamente con los métodos clásicos", so the "alone" now attaches to the comparison ("compared only with") rather than to classical-only methods. "La corrección del resultado" in [4] can be misread as error correction in a course about error correction, and [9] has a clumsy "Para un enfoque simplificado para aprovechar". Otherwise the page is faithful, uses tú ("consulta", "ayudarte") and keeps its terms consistent (disparos, tolerante a fallos, supresión/mitigación).

examples.line_approx: Mientras tanto, formas cada vez más avanzadas...
examples.source: increasingly advanced forms of error correction are steadily coming within reach
examples.translation: formas cada vez más avanzadas de corrección de errores están al alcance de la mano
examples.suggested: formas cada vez más avanzadas de corrección de errores se van poniendo a nuestro alcance de forma constante
examples.why: The English says this is gradual progress, but the translation says it is already here. That overstates how mature error correction is today.

examples.line_approx: El cálculo demuestre una separación cuántica
examples.source: compared with classical methods alone
examples.translation: en comparación únicamente con los métodos clásicos
examples.suggested: en comparación con los métodos clásicos por sí solos
examples.why: 'únicamente' is in the wrong place. It now limits the comparison ('compared only with') instead of saying the baseline is classical methods on their own.

examples.line_approx: La corrección del resultado se pueda verificar
examples.source: The correctness of the output can be rigorously verified.
examples.translation: La corrección del resultado se pueda verificar rigurosamente.
examples.suggested: La validez (o exactitud) del resultado se pueda verificar rigurosamente.
examples.why: In a course about error correction, 'corrección' can be read as 'correction' rather than 'correctness'.

examples.line_approx: Para un enfoque simplificado para aprovechar...
examples.source: For a streamlined approach to leveraging multiple error mitigation techniques
examples.translation: Para un enfoque simplificado para aprovechar múltiples técnicas
examples.suggested: Si buscas un enfoque simplificado que combine varias técnicas de mitigación de errores
examples.why: Two 'para' in a row reads as a calque of the English.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. I found no inverted condition or hallucinated claim: the T1, SPAM, coherent-vs-incoherent, Kraus-channel and error-propagation passages all match the English. The problems are all minor. "Quantum computer" switches from "computadora cuántica" (most of the file) to "ordenador cuántico" in [242] and [256]. "Dephasing" appears as both "desfasaje" [165] and "desfase" [211] onward. A few sentences are calqued or clumsy: "requirió casi ninguna puerta" [73], "podrían valer la pena suprimirlos" [61], "pueden modelarse mediante puertas unitarias, ellos mismos" [106]. In [276], "moved past" became "pasar por alto", which normally means "overlook/ignore", where "pasar a través de" or "mover más allá" (the rendering in [277]) is meant. Separately, [96] translates a LaTeX subscript (p_\text{noisy} → p_\text{ruidosa}) inside the math.

examples.source: meaning the error could be simply "moved past" the CNOT without having any effect on other qubits
examples.translation: el error podría simplemente "pasar por alto" la CNOT
examples.suggested: el error podría simplemente "desplazarse más allá de" la CNOT
examples.why: "Pasar por alto" means to overlook/ignore. That muddies the commutation idea, and [277] already renders the same concept as "mover más allá".

examples.source: IBM quantum computers implement abstract two-qubit gates
examples.translation: Los ordenadores cuánticos de IBM implementan
examples.suggested: Las computadoras cuánticas de IBM implementan
examples.why: The rest of the file uses "computadora cuántica". Here and in [256] it switches to the Peninsular "ordenador".

examples.source: This first visualization of error required almost no gates other than delays
examples.translation: Esta primera visualización del error requirió casi ninguna puerta aparte de los retardos
examples.suggested: Esta primera visualización del error prácticamente no requirió puertas, aparte de los retardos
examples.why: "Requirió casi ninguna" is a calque of "required almost no" and is ungrammatical in Spanish.

examples.source: T1 errors might still be worth suppressing at much shorter times
examples.translation: los errores de $T_1$ podrían valer la pena suprimirlos incluso en tiempos mucho más cortos
examples.suggested: podría valer la pena suprimir los errores de $T_1$ incluso en tiempos mucho más cortos
examples.why: Broken agreement and a dangling clitic. Understandable, but no native writer would phrase it this way.

examples.source: can be modeled by unitary gates, themselves
examples.translation: pueden modelarse mediante puertas unitarias, ellos mismos
examples.suggested: pueden modelarse, a su vez, mediante puertas unitarias
examples.why: "Ellos mismos" is a literal calque of the English emphatic "themselves" and reads as robotic.

examples.source: Dephasing (loss of phase information)
examples.translation: Desfasaje (pérdida de información de fase)
examples.suggested: Desfase (pérdida de información de fase)
examples.why: From [211] on, the file uses "desfase" / "canal de desfase", so this term is inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: All three entries are faithful and use the informal tú register, e.g. "Continúa tu viaje de aprendizaje" and "rutas de aprendizaje en IBM Quantum Platform"; the short "¡Lección próximamente!" is a fair rendering of the placeholder notice.

The translation is faithful and natural. It uses "tú" throughout, and the exam terms are exact: "debes responder correctamente al menos 16 para aprobar", "el examen se bloqueará temporalmente" after two failed attempts, and the Credly data-sharing notice is rendered completely.

All four short entries are faithful and read naturally, including 'Simulación clásica', 'El módulo está disponible en GitHub' and 'se considera opcional, pero es muy recomendable', which is a defensible rendering of 'can be considered optional'.

Entry 48 is faithful and natural. "Para más detalles sobre las opciones de mitigación de errores, consulta las siguientes guías y la referencia de la API" keeps the informal tú form ("consulta"), and the link labels match entry 42 ("Configurar la mitigación de errores").

Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. Entry 21 keeps the non-commuting condition and its consequence ("no conmutan… no pueden reordenarse en la serie de Taylor… es un desafío"), and entry 50 uses a natural "Contemos las operaciones de este circuito", in line with "Hamiltoniano" and "puertas cuánticas" elsewhere in the file.
